TV Time shut down last month, and now one of its co-founders, Antonio Pinto, has announced the launch of a brand-new TV and film tracking app called Bingers, further enhancing its social features. Here's what you need to know.

Bingers is now available for download

After Whip Media announced the closure of TV Time, one of its co-founders promptly launched Bingers, positioning it as "a fast, good-looking watchlist with a fun community."

According to TechCrunch, Bingers is already available for download on iOS and Android platforms, offering a sense of continuity for users who have yet to find an alternative. TV Time was once one of the most widely used TV and film tracking apps globally.

Former users who previously saved their data through the TV Time export tool can import their records into Bingers and pick up right where they left off. As for those who never exported their data, or newcomers to TV and film tracking apps, they can start fresh from scratch.

Bingers places a strong emphasis on community features, including user profiles, comments, episode ratings, GIFs, polls, and character popularity elections. Speaking to TechCrunch, Pinton noted that these were precisely the features that kept users coming back to TV Time:

If you simply want to keep track of what you've watched, Bingers offers a dedicated watchlist and viewing history. Just like TV Time, it also features a calendar function that displays upcoming episodes and premiere dates, along with a countdown to when new content becomes available.

Bingers is available for free download on the App Store and currently has no in-app purchases.
